notes: Schema 2. `epochs` lists configuration epochs: a new one starts whenever SimConfig changes or 'New epoch' is pressed (at most 16 are kept, shortest finished ones dropped first). Everything inside an epoch was measured under that epoch's `config`, so epochs can be compared with each other but must never be averaged together. `step` is the wall time of one whole Simulation::step and is the root: there is no root span label. Each entry of `spans` is a timed code section: `calls` is how often it ran, `calls_per_step` its cadence (3 = once per substep), and `per_step_ms` its total time per simulation step. Compare labels by `per_step_ms` (or total_ms), never by mean_call_ms, which is per call and so not comparable across different cadences. Spans nest by '::' prefix (a::b::c is inside a::b when that label exists) and otherwise sit directly under `step`; a span's share of the step is per_step_ms / step.mean_ms, and nested spans must not be summed. `counters` count work done. A counter 'owner::unit' applies to the span 'owner' and every span nested under it, and is emitted once per call of 'owner'; a span's `per_unit` then gives nanoseconds per unit of work (e.g. per neighbour), which separates slower code from a heavier workload. `ns_per_particle_per_call` divides a span's mean call time by the epoch's particle_count. `recorder` is a flight recorder of the last `len` steps, oldest first, across epochs (`epoch_ids` says which epoch each step belongs to): `step_ms` is the whole step, `span_ms[label]` the summed time of that span within the step, `counters[label]` the summed count. min/max are single-call extremes and include startup outliers; use the recorder to look at spikes. Spans averaging under about 2 microseconds are at the timer's resolution (around 100 ns on Windows) and their decimals are noise. Not recorded: render/GPU time, wall-clock duration, release vs debug optimisation level.
